About

I'm a communications all-rounder with 8 years of working across four continents. I don't fit neatly into one lane — I never have. I've built complete communications functions from scratch, authored two-year coalition strategies, designed annual reports, written donor narratives, run BBC-covered advocacy campaigns, created social media content calendars, and pulled the analytics to prove what worked. All of it.

Rooted in the Global South, I've worked with governments, grassroots NGOs, international development organisations, LGBTQ+ advocacy groups, education nonprofits, and for-profit brands across India, the US, the UK, Australia, Africa, and the Middle East. The context changes. The commitment to doing it properly doesn't.

I'm as comfortable in a strategy session as I am in a Canva file, a press pitch, or a data dashboard.

"The most powerful communications don't find the right approach — they find the unexpected one. The one that makes an unheard voice impossible to ignore."

Case Study — The work in depth
Dost Education
Early Childhood Development · Non-profit · India / US · Reported to CEO
StrategyBrand identityCampaignsAnnual ReportAnalyticsAdvocacy2022–2025
01 — The situation
No comms infrastructure. At all.
Dost had a clear mission and real impact — but no brand guidelines, no messaging framework, no digital presence, no strategy. Everything was inconsistent. They needed someone to build it from zero, not inherit something broken.
02 — What I built
The entire infrastructure.
Brand guidelines and visual identity. Messaging frameworks for parents, funders, and government partners. The first Annual Report, end-to-end. All social media content and strategy. The 'Talk, Care & Play' advocacy campaign. Partnership comms for UNICEF and LEGO Foundation.
03 — What changed
A brand that earned its place.
Consistent platform growth across all channels month on month. An annual report that secured funder confidence. International visibility through UNICEF and LEGO. A comms function that ran independently after I moved on.
